lead: The seven lessons become a program: in 90 days, one to three managers take one tool each from the map to the handoff to IT, with fixed meetings and milestones you can check. At the end, the final project at Horizonte and the dashboard of what changed in the market this quarter.
objetivo: build the 90-day plan with meetings, milestones, and indicators for a real manager and deliver the final project.

aprende.t: The five phases of the program

hero_alt: A mentor sticks colored notes on a twelve-week calendar on the wall while the manager watches.

secoes.sub: Each phase ends with a milestone. Click each block.

nos.detalhe: Kickoff workshop with the owner and the managers, an inventory of what's already in use, and a mapping session with each manager (lesson 1). Milestone: each manager has chosen one tool, with its risk.
Filter and spec (lesson 2), prototyping session with fictional data (lesson 3). Milestone: prototype running on the manager's computer, with gaps noted.
Constitution applied (lesson 4), test suite and rounds (lesson 5). Milestone: test suite at 85% or higher and no limit violated.
User acceptance testing and handoff package with IT review (lessons 5 and 6). Milestone: IT decision recorded and shutdown test done.
Dashboard with baseline, weekly reviews, and one tested improvement (lesson 7). Milestone: closing meeting with the owner, with numbers and the decision on the next cycle.

secoes.volta: Next cycle: new tool or new manager
secoes.legenda: One manager per tool. One to three managers per program, so the mentor can deliver with quality.

rolagem_fim.texto: Map, spec and prototype, limits and tests, acceptance testing and handoff, measure and decide. Five milestones, one every two or three weeks.

secoes.titulo: How to set up and run the program

passos.sub: Who sponsors, who builds, who validates
texto: Sponsor: the owner (Carlos) opens doors and decides at the end. Managers: build and own the processes. IT: validates and takes over. Mentor: leads the method and the pace.
Also choose one reference user per tool, who will use it every day and say whether it feels comfortable.

exemplo.texto: Patrícia (follow-up), Juliana (ready-made customer service replies), and Rafael in IT.

texto: One 60-minute weekly meeting per manager, always on the same day. Plus the long prototyping and acceptance testing sessions on the right dates.
Between meetings, the manager has a task with a "done when". Without a task, the program turns into conversation.

exemplo.texto: A missed milestone changes the date of the next one, never the criterion.

texto: Each phase closes with something anyone can check: the map table, the prototype opening, the test suite with a score, the IT decision, the dashboard with a baseline.
On day 90, a meeting with the owner: what changed in the numbers, what it costs, what comes in the next cycle.

exemplo.texto: "Do we continue, expand, or stop? Based on what?"

texto: Build the 90-day plan for Horizonte for Patrícia and Juliana, and deliver the eight completed templates for the follow-up tool.
Use the lab pieces to show what the program prevents: each failure F1 to F12 must appear in some control in your plan.

exemplo.texto: The INEMA certification for each program is coming soon. It is a qualification, not a regulated profession.

secoes.sub: Copy and adjust the dates to your manager.

Alerts: milestone 2 weeks late -> meeting with the sponsor · limit violated -> pause.

FINAL PROJECT · AI Mentor · lab company: Horizonte Distribuidora

Submit in one folder (or repository) with:
1. Map of Patrícia's 3 tools, with risk (lesson 1)
2. One-page spec for the follow-up, with permissions and excluded data (lesson 2)
3. Prototyping session script + AGENTS.md + lacunas.md (lesson 3)
4. Constitution for the follow-up agent (lesson 4)
5. Test suite of 15 cases with expected answers and one scored round (lesson 5)
6. Handoff package for Rafael + IT review checklist (lesson 6)
7. Dashboard of 3 indicators with a baseline + 1 hypothesis card (lesson 7)
8. 90-day plan for Patrícia and Juliana (this lesson)

Done when:
- no template has a field between < > left blank
- each lab failure (F1 to F12) appears in at least one control
  in your templates, with the line indicated
- customer data used: fictional only

abas.html:
• F1–F4: IT review checklist (lesson 6).
  • F5–F7: limits and permissions in the constitution (lesson 4) and critical cases in the test suite (lesson 5).
  • F8, F10: fictional data in the prototype (lesson 3) and the data block of the package (lesson 6).
  • F9: least permission in the integrations (lesson 6).
  • F11: dashboard baseline (lesson 7).
  • F12: week 1 inventory (lessons 1 and 8).

• Five managers in the first program: the mentor can't follow along with quality.
  • Milestone with no criterion: "prototype almost ready" is not a milestone.
  • Skipping day 90: without a decision from the owner, the program fades out with no result.

itens.texto: Oct/2026: OpenAI brought GPT-6 to everyone in ChatGPT, on free and paid plans. The manager can prototype without a new license; the care with real data stays the same. OpenAI, Deployment Safety Hub

itens.t: An agent that uses the computer
itens.texto: Sep/2026: Claude Code started using the computer in the background in the desktop app (beta, Pro and Max plans). More power calls for more limits: per-action permissions matter even more. Claude Code, week 36 news
09/22/2026: Anthropic launched Opus 5.5, which it says costs 40% less than Opus 5 on typical tasks. Run the test suite with the new model before switching. Anthropic
Announced on 06/03/2026: OpenAI's Agent Builder goes offline on 11/30/2026. That is why the handoff package keeps rules, code, and access outside the tool. OpenAI, deprecations

itens.t: Security scanning in the coding agent
itens.texto: 2026: the Codex documentation now includes repository security scanning. It helps Rafael, but it does not replace the IT review or the penetration test. Codex changelog

itens.t: A harder entry into a career
itens.texto: 08/12/2026: Stanford estimates that employment for ages 22 to 25 in the occupations most exposed to AI is 19% lower than it would have been had it tracked that of peers in less exposed occupations; the study does not claim a cause. Mentoring and programs like this one gain weight. Stanford Digital Economy Lab

secoes.sub: Four questions about the whole program.

perguntas.p: At what phase of the program does IT decide whether the tool goes into production?
opcoes: Days 56–70, after acceptance testing and the handoff package.
perguntas.explica: IT reviews the package after the user runs acceptance testing. The decision is recorded and the shutdown test is done before going live.

opcoes: The criterion, to fit the deadline.
The date of the next milestone; the criterion stays.
perguntas.explica: A missed milestone changes dates, never the criterion. A two-week delay goes to the sponsor.

perguntas.p: A tool the manager uses is discontinued at the end of the quarter. What protects the company?
opcoes: The handoff package with rules, code and access kept outside the tool.
perguntas.explica: Method and documents survive a change of tool. That is why the tool of the month stays only in this panel.

perguntas.p: How many managers fit in the first program?
opcoes: One to three, one per tool.
All the managers in the company.
perguntas.explica: One to three lets you follow each session and each milestone with quality.
